summary: A twelve-day private journey from Addis Ababa through Rift Valley lakes, Arba Minch, Dorze, Konso, Jinka and the Omo lowlands, returning through coffee country. The road is part of the story, with respectful cultural visits, wildlife time and careful pacing.
overview: A twelve-day private journey through the changing landscapes and cultures of Southern Ethiopia — not a tribal checklist. Travellers move from Rift Valley lakes to mountain highlands, Konso terraces, Omo lowlands, pastoral communities and the Omo River, then return through coffee country and the Rift toward Addis Ababa. The road itself is part of the experience.
heroAccent: Where the road becomes part of the story.
style: Private / Premium / Cultural / Wildlife / Landscape / Photography
difficulty: Easy to Moderate (long road days; short walks; heat in lowlands)
fit: Travellers who want thoughtful southern travel with local knowledge and respectful cultural tourism.
imageAlt: Southern Ethiopia landscapes and road journey
notice: Road, weather, river, park, market and community conditions can change the programme. Ceremonies, wildlife, markets and specific encounters are never guaranteed.
itineraryIntro: Premium private pacing gives important bases two nights, leaves room for community context and treats people as hosts rather than attractions. Photography requires consent.
introduction: Lake Chamo boat time, Dorze and Guge highlands, Konso terraces, Jinka and Mago, a multi-night Turmi base, Karo and Omo River landscapes, Omorate and Dassanech visits, then coffee country and the Rift Valley return.

highlights.body: Lake Chamo boat time when weather and operations allow; wildlife sightings are never guaranteed.
Dorze / Guge Mountains highland culture, architecture, agriculture and food where arranged.
Konso UNESCO cultural landscape of terraces, stone walls and farming systems.
Jinka museum or research context before the Mago and Omo days, when open.
Mago National Park and the Mursi area subject to current road and park conditions.
Key Afer market only when it is operating; Turmi base for slower Hamer, Karo and Omorate days.
Southern coffee country and Rift Valley return, with private vehicle, professional guide and local specialists where required.

preparation: Expect long road days and heat in the lowlands.
Pack sun protection, comfortable walking shoes, layers and reusable water capacity.
Photography of people requires permission; ceremonies and specific encounters are never promised.
Final routing, meal plan and operating conditions are confirmed in the written quotation.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa → Arba Minch
itinerary.subtitle: Day 1
paragraphs: Morning departure from Addis through changing Rift Valley landscapes. Selected cultural or archaeological stops may be possible according to departure time and road conditions.
Arrive in Arba Minch, check in and rest. Optional sunset overlooking the lakes when weather cooperates.
notes: The landscape begins changing before the traveller reaches the south.

itinerary.title: Lakes, Wildlife & Dorze
itinerary.subtitle: Day 2
paragraphs: Early Lake Chamo boat excursion, subject to weather and operations, looking for crocodiles, hippos, waterbirds and fish eagles without sighting guarantees.
After lunch, climb into the Guge Mountains toward Dorze for architecture, weaving, agriculture, food and highland adaptation. Return to Arba Minch.

itinerary.title: Arba Minch → Konso
itinerary.subtitle: Day 3
paragraphs: Travel through the Rift toward Konso. Explore the UNESCO cultural landscape of terraces, stone walls, traditional settlements and farming systems.
Where practical, stay somewhere that lets guests experience the surrounding landscape rather than only a town room.

itinerary.title: Konso → Jinka
itinerary.subtitle: Day 4
paragraphs: Continue south with possible stops according to timing and local conditions. A market visit is included only when a real market is operating.
In Jinka, visit the South Omo Research Center or local museum when open to establish cultural context before the Omo days.

itinerary.title: Jinka → Mago → Mursi Area → Jinka
itinerary.subtitle: Day 5
paragraphs: Enter Mago National Park and the Mursi area subject to current road and park conditions. Focus on livelihood, cattle, agriculture, social traditions, environment, history and change.
Return to Jinka for a slower afternoon with local coffee or a selected community experience when available. Photography requires permission; local life is not a performance.

itinerary.title: Jinka → Key Afer → Turmi
itinerary.subtitle: Day 6
paragraphs: Travel toward Turmi and stop at Key Afer market only when the operating day has been confirmed. Continue through changing Omo landscapes.
After check-in, a nearby Hamer community visit may be arranged for daily life, livestock, craft, food and conversation.

itinerary.title: Hamer Cultural Day
itinerary.subtitle: Day 7
paragraphs: Spend a slower day with a locally arranged Hamer visit focused on pastoral life, agriculture, family life, craft, clothing, livestock and food.
Music, dance or a genuine ceremony may be observed only when naturally occurring, appropriate and welcome. Afternoon is for consented photography, rest or a local walk.

itinerary.title: Karo & Omo River
itinerary.subtitle: Day 8
paragraphs: Travel toward the Omo River and Karo area. Where locally arranged, explore river life, agriculture, cattle, art and environmental adaptation.
Continue to Omo viewpoints where access allows, then return toward Turmi. The river is treated as a living landscape that has shaped movement and livelihood for generations.

itinerary.title: Omorate & Dassanech
itinerary.subtitle: Day 9
paragraphs: Early departure toward Omorate. Boat crossing or local transport is used where required and operating.
Visit a Dassanech community through local arrangements to understand river environment, pastoralism, fishing or agriculture, craft and changing livelihoods. Return toward Turmi.

itinerary.title: Turmi → Konso / Yirgalem
itinerary.subtitle: Day 10
paragraphs: Begin north without treating the day as a single transfer. Break the journey where practical through changing landscapes.
A coffee experience may be possible according to the final route and local availability.

itinerary.title: Coffee, Forest & Rift Valley
itinerary.subtitle: Day 11
paragraphs: Visit a coffee-growing area or local coffee experience where available, covering farming, harvesting, processing, preparation and coffee culture.
Continue through the Rift Valley with a possible Ziway or Langano stop according to routing.

itinerary.title: Return to Addis Ababa
itinerary.subtitle: Day 12
paragraphs: Continue toward Addis with scenic stops when time allows. Arrive for airport transfer and the end of the journey.

itineraryNotes: Road conditions, weather, river levels, park access, market days and local community activities can change the plan.
Guests ask before photographing people. Wildlife, ceremonies and specific village experiences are never guaranteed.
Final routing and meal plan are confirmed in the quotation.

summary: A four-day private wildlife and highland-nature extension after The Southern Ethiopia Journey, moving from Dinsho forest approaches to the Sanetti Plateau and Harenna Forest before returning toward Addis.
overview: For travellers who want wildlife and high mountains after the Omo Valley. Bale Mountains National Park adds a completely different ecosystem: Afro-alpine plateau, Ethiopian wolf habitat on Sanetti, Dinsho forest approaches and Harenna cloud forest. It is a selected premium add-on, not a rushed checklist.
heroAccent: A different ecosystem after the Omo lowlands.
fit: Guests finishing the southern journey who want nature contrast before flying out of Addis.
notice: Wildlife sightings are never guaranteed. Sanetti altitude, weather, trails and road access require flexible pacing.
itineraryIntro: Attaches to The Southern Ethiopia Journey and is priced and planned with the main programme.
introduction: Bale combines volcanic peaks, Afro-alpine moorland, Ethiopian wolf habitat, Dinsho wildlife and Harenna cloud forest in one focused add-on.

highlights.body: UNESCO Bale Mountains ecological zones.
Dinsho wildlife and forest introduction.
Sanetti Plateau high-altitude landscapes and Ethiopian wolf habitat.
Harenna Forest before the return toward Addis.

preparation: Bring layers, sun protection, sturdy shoes and water capacity.
Allow slower pacing at Sanetti altitude.
Routes and vehicle sections adapt to fitness and weather.

itinerary.title: Toward Bale
itinerary.subtitle: Day 1
paragraphs: Travel toward Bale Mountains from the southern or Rift routing and settle into the park area according to the final plan.

itinerary.title: Dinsho / Wildlife
itinerary.subtitle: Day 2
paragraphs: Guided time around Dinsho with forest walks, highland vegetation and wildlife observation in known habitats. Sightings are not guaranteed.

itinerary.title: Sanetti Plateau
itinerary.subtitle: Day 3
paragraphs: High-altitude day on Sanetti: open moorland, thin air and Ethiopian wolf habitat. Walking and vehicle sections adapt to fitness and weather.

itinerary.title: Harenna Forest / Return
itinerary.subtitle: Day 4
paragraphs: Spend time in Harenna Forest on Bale’s southern slopes, then begin the return toward Addis Ababa for an airport or city transfer.

itineraryNotes: The extension is planned with the main southern journey.
Park trails, weather and road access can change the plan.

tourName: Northern Ethiopia — The Long Way North
summary: A twelve-day private progression from Lake Tana and Bahir Dar through royal Gondar, Simien mountain country, Lalibela’s sacred stone and Axum’s ancient empire.
overview: Most northern tours simply connect famous destinations. This private journey is designed as a progression: Lake → Kingdom → Mountain → Sacred Stone → Ancient Empire. Travellers move through Explore Ethiopia with enough time in each chapter, guided by a Gondar-based team and flexible domestic connections.
heroAccent: From sacred waters to royal cities and mountain country.
style: Private / Premium / Cultural / Historical / Mountain / Local
difficulty: Moderate (Simien walks; some long transfer and flight days)
fit: Travellers who want a coherent Explore Ethiopia journey rather than a five-stop checklist.
imageAlt: Northern Ethiopia highland and historic landscapes
notice: Domestic flights, road links, weather, park access and site opening times are confirmed against current conditions. Day 7 protects the experience over forced connections.
itineraryIntro: Lake → Kingdom → Mountain → Sacred Stone → Ancient Empire. Gondar is home and Simien is the specialty; the wider north is connected through local knowledge and private pacing.
introduction: Bahir Dar and Lake Tana open the journey, royal Gondar and Simien deepen it, Lalibela provides sacred stone and Axum closes the story as ancient empire.

highlights.body: Bahir Dar and Lake Tana monasteries, with boat access conditions respected.
Optional Blue Nile Falls when season, road access and time allow.
A full royal Gondar day with Fasil Ghebbi and selected heritage sites.
Two nights in Simien with escarpment walking and wildlife time.
Two nights in Lalibela for an introduction and deeper second day.
A full historic Axum day focused on the story of the kingdom.

preparation: Pack layers and comfortable walking shoes for Simien and highland sites.
Allow flexibility for domestic flight and road schedules.
Respect religious sites, services and photography rules.
Optional Gheralta or Ras Dashen extensions are planned separately.

itinerary.title: Addis Ababa → Bahir Dar
itinerary.subtitle: Day 1
paragraphs: Take a domestic flight according to the current schedule. Settle into Bahir Dar with lakefront time, local coffee and rest.

itinerary.title: Lake Tana
itinerary.subtitle: Day 2
paragraphs: Travel by boat to selected monastery and church sites according to access and operations. Learn about Orthodox traditions, monastic history, art and lake culture.
Blue Nile Falls is an optional afternoon visit when season and road access allow.

itinerary.title: Bahir Dar → Gondar
itinerary.subtitle: Day 3
paragraphs: Drive through changing highland landscapes to Gondar. Settle in and take a local orientation walk or coffee stop.

itinerary.title: Royal Gondar
itinerary.subtitle: Day 4
paragraphs: Spend a full guided day at Fasil Ghebbi, Debre Berhan Selassie and selected historic locations according to opening and access. Prepare for Simien.

itinerary.title: Gondar → Simien
itinerary.subtitle: Day 5
paragraphs: Travel via Debark for park arrangements and enter Simien. Take first viewpoints and a short acclimatisation walk; wildlife is never guaranteed.

itinerary.title: Simien Mountains
itinerary.subtitle: Day 6
paragraphs: Spend a full mountain day on a route through Sankaber, Geech, Jinbar or selected escarpment viewpoints according to the final trek plan.

itinerary.title: Simien → Gondar / onward connection
itinerary.subtitle: Day 7
paragraphs: Enjoy a final mountain experience and return toward Gondar. Continue toward Lalibela only when transport allows; otherwise protect the experience with an overnight in Gondar.

itinerary.title: Lalibela
itinerary.subtitle: Day 8
paragraphs: Arrive and begin an introduction to the rock-hewn churches according to opening times and local planning.

itinerary.title: Lalibela Deep Experience
itinerary.subtitle: Day 9
paragraphs: Use a full second day for churches, architecture, religious history and living practice. An early service is included only where appropriate and welcome.

itinerary.title: Lalibela → Axum
itinerary.subtitle: Day 10
paragraphs: Travel by the appropriate current transport, confirmed closer to travel. Arrive in Axum and rest with an optional evening walk.

itinerary.title: Historic Axum
itinerary.subtitle: Day 11
paragraphs: Explore stelae, archaeology, religious heritage, the St Mary of Zion area where access is available and local history. The story of Axum matters more than a monument checklist.

itinerary.title: Axum → Addis Ababa
itinerary.subtitle: Day 12
paragraphs: Transfer for the morning flight according to schedule and connect onward from Addis.

itineraryNotes: The product name remains Northern Ethiopia — The Long Way North while the site section is Explore Ethiopia.
Roads, flights, weather, park access and opening times can change the programme.
Wildlife, services, Blue Nile Falls appearance and summit goals are never guaranteed.

summary: A two or three-day private extension through Gheralta’s sandstone cliffs, mesas and selected rock-hewn churches when security, road access and fitness make travel appropriate.
overview: Gheralta adds sandstone cliffs, mesa country, remote rock churches and local guiding to an Explore Ethiopia journey. Church approaches can be steep and exact sites depend on current access, weather and operational safety.
heroAccent: Sandstone cliffs and sacred places, carefully planned.
difficulty: Moderate to Challenging (steep church approaches; fitness dependent)
fit: Travellers adding a conditions-dependent landscape and heritage chapter from Axum or a wider northern route.
imageAlt: Gheralta sandstone cliffs and rock churches in Tigray
notice: Only offered when current security, road access and operations make travel appropriate. Exact churches are confirmed close to travel.
itineraryIntro: This is an optional extension, never a fixed public checklist or guaranteed part of the base Long Way North journey.
introduction: Gheralta feels unlike Simien’s escarpments or Lalibela’s town churches: sandstone cliffs, flat-topped mesas and elevated churches reached by demanding approaches.

highlights.body: Gheralta / Geralta cliff and mesa landscapes.
Selected Tigray rock churches where access and fitness allow.
Local specialist guiding for steep approaches.
Photography of stone churches in elevated settings.

preparation: Expect steep approaches and uneven ground.
Bring modest clothing and follow church photography rules.
Final churches, roads and overnight locations are confirmed close to travel.

summary: A five to seven-day serious Simien trekking extension that replaces the compact mountain section of The Long Way North with a Ras Dashen-oriented route and high-altitude camping.
overview: For fit trekkers who want serious mountain time inside the Explore Ethiopia journey. The standard two-day Simien block is replaced by a five to seven-day Ras Dashen-oriented extension, changing difficulty, length, logistics and cost. Summit success is never guaranteed.
heroAccent: A longer mountain journey inside the northern story.
difficulty: Challenging to Demanding (high altitude; summit not guaranteed)
fit: Fit trekkers with altitude awareness who accept a demanding, flexible mountain programme.
imageAlt: Ras Dashen trekking landscape in the Simien Mountains
notice: This is priced and planned separately. Weather, health, route conditions and group fitness can turn back a summit attempt.
itineraryIntro: The add-on changes the base journey substantially: downstream Lalibela and Axum dates move later and domestic flights must be rebuilt.

summary: A seven-day private running journey through Gondar and the Simien Mountains, built around trail and mountain running with routes adapted to ability, altitude, weather and current trail conditions.
overview: Ethiopia is famous for runners; this is a running journey through Gondar and the Simien Mountains, not a sightseeing tour with a short jog added. Guests run through the historic city, into the highlands and on mountain trails above the escarpment, with coffee stops and time among people who live in the landscape.
heroAccent: Run the land. Meet the people. Know the mountains.
style: Private running journey / Trail & mountain running / Local guiding
difficulty: Easy Runner to Ultra (routes adapted to ability)
fit: Recreational, trail and experienced mountain runners who want Gondar and Simien at running pace.
imageAlt: Trail running in the Simien Mountains
notice: This is not a race and not a standard trek rebadged as running. Distances and trails change with weather, park requirements, altitude and runner ability.
itineraryIntro: Before travel we ask about recent mileage, longest recent run, trail experience, altitude experience, preferred distance, dates and whether the priority is sightseeing, training or both.

introduction: This is dirt trails, uneven ground, climbs, descents and altitude with a guide who knows the mountains, communities and terrain. Geladas and other wildlife may be encountered on their terms.

highlights.body: Signature seven-day Gondar and Simien running journey.
City and countryside running before mountain trail days.
Possible routes around Sankaber, Geech, Imet Gogo and Chenek selected by conditions and ability.
Flexible distances, wildlife without chasing it, coffee and local encounters.

preparation: Share running background, weekly mileage, longest recent run and trail experience.
Discuss altitude experience, preferred distance and training goals.
Bring personal running shoes, kit, layers, hydration and sun protection.
Expect uneven ground, climbs, descents and changing altitude.
